newsitem.title: USA: Appeal filed in Tampa, Fla., Bucs bond case.
newsitem.headline: Appeal filed in Tampa, Fla., Bucs bond case.

text.p: Former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe has appealed the Florida Supreme Court's validation of $204.5 million of revenue bonds for the Buccaneers new stadium.
There has been no decision yet on whether to delay the bond sale, an assistant to the Tampa Sports Authority's executive director said Tuesday. Pricing is set for next week via Smith Barney.

Poe filed his request for a rehearing with the state Supreme Court late Monday, just minutes before the appeal deadline expired. The court clerk said there had been no ruling on the request Tuesday, and no hearing scheduled.
Poe has argued that the project would unconstitutionally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit football team.

The Florida Supreme Court unanimously rejected that argument when they validated the bond issue on May 22. The court said local officials acted within their authority when they agreed to build the stadium to keep the team from moving away.

Hillsborough County voters approved a sales tax increase for the stadium and other projects last fall. Construction on the 65,000-seat stadium began immediately, but without the bond proceeds, the county and City of Tampa will have only enough money to continue construction through July 1.
